**Test Image Analysis:**
- **Plant part affected:** Soybean pods
- **Key features:** Tan/brown discolored pods with reduced fill and shriveled appearance; green stems; multiple pods showing similar symptoms; papery texture to pods

This suggests seed/pod disease, likely involving infection affecting seed development or quality. Let me compare with reference images.

**Comparison Analysis:**

- **Phomopsis:** Reference shows tan/brown discolored pods with lesions and shriveled appearance - matches test image very closely
- **White Mold:** Characteristic white fluffy growth and black sclerotia not present in test image
- **Purple Seed Stain:** Would show pink/purple seed discoloration - test image shows tan/brown, not purple
- **Sudden Death Syndrome:** Primarily affects roots and shows characteristic leaf vein necrosis - not evident here
- **Bean Pod Mottle Virus:** Would show mottled leaf symptoms - not visible in test image
- **Charcoal Rot:** Would show black specks/microsclerotia on stems - not evident here

**Key diagnostic features in test image:**
- Multiple tan/brown discolored pods with reduced fill
- Papery, shriveled seed appearance
- Lesion-like discoloration on pod surfaces
- No white fungal growth or sclerotia
- Healthy green stems

This presentation is most consistent with **Phomopsis**, which causes infected seeds to become "cracked, shriveled, dull" with possible "gray mold" on seeds.
